description: NIST's CTC-01 (the committed real/nist-ctc-01), solid #101: the crease e290 where two equal cylinders f85 and f86 whose axes meet cross, an ellipse, filleted at r 1.910, the battery's radius from its sample. At v211 the two cylinders are tangent to each other and to the plane f68 across: the ball there touches both at the vertex, and the walked stripe (ADR-0062) narrows to it, a pole of its surface, the vertex kept. At v113 the crease runs on tangent into the vertical corner e130 between two planes each tangent to one cylinder, a vertex of four edges (ADR-0039 §1), and the fillet goes on down it as a cylinder. Open CASCADE builds the same faces with the same pole, its contacts missing the ball by 5.3e-4 at the median of 200 samples a contact and 2.2e-3 at worst, where Arris' miss it by 5.0e-10 and 7.8e-10: the 8.6e-4 its blend face's area lies from Arris' and each cylinder's 1.7e-2 mm² the other way. Over the part that is 5.5e-9 of its area and 9e-10 of its volume, which the measure tolerances cover under ADR-0062's 1e-5 for a walked fixture (no closed form holds the blend). The counts differ by the part as read (plans/nurbs-face-blend steps 1 and 9b)

analytic.counts_differ: the part as read: Open CASCADE's healed reading of solid #101 splits two edges at (±30, -80, -35), two vertices and two edges more than Arris reads (real/nist-ctc-01, occt_heals); the fillet adds the same to both, two vertices, four edges and two faces
